consensus_summary: Almond primarily symbolizes God’s watchfulness/vigilance over His word via the Jeremiah 1:11-12 shaqed/shoqed wordplay and early blooming; common complementary strands are Aaron’s rod (election/priesthood, sometimes resurrection) and menorah almond cups (sanctuary light), plus Ecclesiastes old-age imagery.
book_summary: Almond is the watcher-tree picturing watchfulness, the sign of the chosen Levitical priesthood via Aaron’s fruitful rod, and the almond cups carrying the sanctuary lamps.
consensus_core_identification: God’s watchfulness (Jeremiah wordplay + early waking), with priesthood and menorah light as standard secondary associations
book_core_identification: watcher-tree (watchfulness) together with sign of chosen Levitical priesthood and sanctuary-lamp cups
boundary_disagreement: None material; book simply co-lists the consensus primary with its two chief alternatives without redefining boundaries or dropping the watchfulness core.
rationale: Minimum cores identify the same referents from the same three texts; consensus already treats priesthood and menorah strands as common and complementary rather than rivals, so the book’s compact conjunction is wording/emphasis difference only, not a changed identification or extension.
strongest_objection: Consensus notes uniformly elevate watchfulness as primary while book coordinates it equally with the other two, which a strict prioritization reading might see as slight re-weighting.
